headline: Every major above its 200-day line and RSI pinned near 80: a strong tape, and a stretched one
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is unusually clean today. All seven majors sit above their 50 and 200-day lines except DOGE and ADA, and even those two are up on every window quoted. BTC is up 25.8% on the week and 21.6% on the month, ETH up 33.6% on the week, SOL up 36.6% on the week. This is not a market split between winners and losers, it is a market where the argument is only about degree. BTC itself is up a modest 0.7% on the day, so the daily candle looks sleepy next to the weekly and monthly numbers, worth separating clearly since they tell different stories: today is quiet, the last month was not.

Momentum is where the picture gets interesting. BTC's RSI-14 is 80.7, ETH's is 77.4, SOL's is 82.8, BNB's is 79.9: these are not merely overbought readings, they are the kind of numbers that show up when a rally has been running long enough to exhaust the easy buyers. MACD is above signal across the board, so trend and momentum currently agree, no divergence to name today. But agreement at these RSI levels is its own kind of information: a market that is unanimously extended is a market with less room to accelerate further before it needs to rest, one way or the other. That is a description of tension, not a forecast of resolution.

Positioning adds a second layer. BTC funding is 4.8% annualized on OKX, ETH 7.9%, SOL 8.4%, XRP a notably rich 11%. These are longs paying shorts to stay in the trade, and the size of the payment scales with how crowded the long side has become. XRP's long/short ratio of 2.45 and DOGE's 3.85 show retail leaning hard into the move even as DOGE funding sits slightly negative at -0.2%, an odd pairing: a crowd of longs on DOGE that isn't (yet) paying up for the privilege. Liquidations over the past day cut both ways, ETH shorts took the bigger hit ($9.0M vs $6.2M in longs wiped out), while XRP and DOGE longs got hurt more than shorts. Open interest is largest in BTC ($2.30B) and ETH ($1.52B), meaning real money is sized into this move, not just noise.

The flow picture directly complicates the sentiment read. Over the last 24 hours, whale wallets moved $169.9M net onto exchanges, driven almost entirely by ETH ($170.2M onto exchanges) while BTC was flat to slightly outbound ($368,724 net off exchanges). Zoom out to the weekly series and the pattern holds: the week ending Aug 05 saw $1.21B move off exchanges, but the three weeks since (Aug 12, Aug 19, Aug 26) have all shown net inflow onto exchanges, most recently $1.36B for the week ending Aug 26. Coins moving toward exchanges during a strong up-move is worth naming plainly: that flow is more consistent with positioning to sell than with accumulation. Meanwhile the ETF tape pulls the other way. BTC spot ETFs saw $5.8M net inflow on Aug 26 and $1,571.5M over the last five sessions, with eight straight days in the same direction; ETH ETFs added $38.3M on the day and $737.2M over five sessions, also eight days running. So traditional-finance demand has been steadily net positive while whale wallets have been net feeding exchanges. Stablecoin float is essentially flat over 30 days (+0.34%), so the dry powder on the sidelines hasn't meaningfully grown to match the rally.

Sentiment sits at 65, Fear & Greed's label reads Greed, comfortably inside its 30-day range of 25 to 74 rather than pinned at the top of it. That is the crowd's mood matching the tape's momentum readings reasonably well this time, no glaring disagreement to lean on. What's worth watching instead: whether the exchange-inflow pattern from whales extends into a fifth straight week, whether BTC's RSI cools from 80.7 without a matching move in price (a divergence that isn't present yet), and whether the ETF inflow streak (eight days running on both BTC and ETH) breaks or holds. Any one of those flipping would change which side of this tension the tape is leaning toward.
